hero.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic and rain to Florida roads
hero.teaser: AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans will have traveled at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, marking an all-time high for the holiday.
hero.body:
A record-breaking number of Americans are hitting the roads this Fourth of July weekend, with Florida experiencing the surge firsthand. AAA estimates that 72.2 million people will travel at least 50 miles from home between June 27 and July 5, marking an all-time high for the holiday. Of those travelers, 61.4 million are driving, making highways across the state increasingly congested. Orlando and Miami have emerged as top five travel destinations for Independence Day, attracting visitors from across the country.

Friday's rainy conditions created challenging driving circumstances on the Florida Turnpike south of Orlando, testing the patience of holiday travelers. Driver Ed Budd described how quickly conditions deteriorated when weather moved in, saying "Really beautiful until it starts raining and then everyone forgets how to drive." The combination of heavy traffic and wet roads created a difficult start to the long weekend for many commuters heading south.

Experiences on the road varied significantly depending on timing and route. Carlos Borras and his wife completed a round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday without incident. "I don't think I saw any traffic, no accidents or anything, so it's been great," Borras said. However, driver Fernando Amado reported much busier conditions along his route. "It's been pretty busy, especially with the weather," Amado said. "I thought people were leaving yesterday, but today is the day when people are really heading up North." The differing experiences highlight how timing and destination significantly impact travel conditions.

For those still planning to travel, AAA offers specific recommendations to avoid peak congestion. Drivers should consider leaving after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday for smoother trips. The heaviest traffic is expected between 10 a.m. and noon on Saturday, and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday. Planning departures strategically around these windows can help travelers avoid the worst delays as millions of Americans make their holiday trips across Florida's roadways.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion Florida budget with $810 million in vetoes
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion state budget this week, marking the fourth consecutive year of shrinking spending plans. The term-limited Governor vetoed nearly $810 million in line-item appropriations, along with blocking another $750 million the Legislature wanted to transfer into the state's rainy-day fund.

DeSantis said he vetoed items he considered either inappropriate or nice to have, declining to match his record-breaking $3.1 billion veto total from 2022. The budget includes billions for accelerating road construction projects, increasing teacher pay, and making major investments in cancer research. The spending plan also sets aside $665 million for Everglades restoration. Among the notable cuts, DeSantis vetoed $91.5 million intended to increase correctional officer salaries.

Government watchdog Florida TaxWatch had urged DeSantis to eliminate 621 projects worth $830 million that the group labeled budget turkeys. DeSantis ultimately vetoed 184 of the 621 appropriations the organization wanted cut. The Legislature passed a proposed constitutional amendment last year that would increase the mandated cap on the budget stabilization fund, prompting lawmakers this year to add the $750 million transfer to prepare for the new requirement.

DeSantis also indicated he would not formally lead any political committee to campaign for a proposed amendment after the Legislature changed his original proposal. He said he might participate if asked but would not spearhead the effort himself. The new fiscal year budget represents DeSantis's final spending plan as Governor.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board challenges judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge Thursday against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectru.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald get his job back, saying "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk, which labeled him as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi, was a "serious offense" and removing him was appropriate.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report obtained by WPTV, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. Theobald, who has taught at Spectrum Academy since 2009, told WPTV the case raises questions about where the line is drawn for teachers speaking outside of school. The school board has final say on reinstatement, with no timeline announced for a decision.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is challenging a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher who was suspended following controversial social media comments about conservative activist Charlie Kirk. Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy who has worked there since 2009, faced discipline after making statements on Facebook that characterized Kirk as racist, misogynistic, and a neo-Nazi.

In a court filing submitted Thursday, the school board disputed Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone's recommendation, arguing that her decision contains findings that lack competent substantial evidence. The board's legal representatives contend that Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk constituted a serious offense that justified his removal from the classroom.

Livingstone's order from the previous month relied on a recent ruling from the Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal, which determined that disciplining teachers for personal Facebook posts created off campus using personal devices and involving no students violated First Amendment protections. The judge recommended not only that Theobald be reinstated but also that he receive back pay and benefits for the time he spent away from his position.

According to an investigation report reviewed by WPTV, Theobald acknowledged writing the comments about Kirk but explained that he had posted them on his mother's private Facebook page as part of a conversation with personal acquaintances. He stated the comments were not intended to reach a broader public audience. Following the judge's recommendation, Theobald discussed the case with WPTV, suggesting it raised broader questions about how schools should define the boundaries of acceptable speech for teachers outside school settings. The school board retains the authority to make a final determination on whether Theobald will be rehired, though no timeline has been established for when that decision will be announced.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Let Late Lead Slip Away in 10-3 Loss to Tarpons
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie Mets were six outs away from ending their losing streak Saturday before a disastrous eighth inning turned a 3-1 lead into a 10-3 loss to the Tampa Tarpons at Clover P
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets were six outs away from ending their losing streak Saturday before a disastrous eighth inning turned a 3-1 lead into a 10-3 loss to the Tampa Tarpons at Clover Park.

Tampa scored six unearned runs in the eighth inning, capitalizing on four Mets errors, then added three more runs in the ninth to pull away on Independence Day. The Tarpons extended their winning streak to eight games, while St. Lucie dropped its ninth straight.

The Mets led 3-1 entering the eighth after building the advantage with timely offense and strong relief work. But Tampa's comeback began after Hans Montero reached and eventually scored the tying run when Bryce Martin-Grudzielanek hit a two-out ground ball to third baseman Branny De Oleo. The ball deflected off De Oleo's glove for an error, allowing Montero to come home and even the game at 3-3.

The inning continued from there, and David McCann delivered the decisive blow with a three-run home run off Conner Ware to give Tampa a 6-3 lead. McCann struck again in the ninth, launching another three-run homer off Luis Alvarez to make it 10-3.

McCann finished 3-for-4 with two home runs, a single, a walk and seven RBI. The performance came one day after he went 0-for-4 with four strikeouts.

St. Lucie had trailed 1-0 early before tying the game in the fourth inning on an RBI groundout by Simon Juan. Chase Meggers gave the Mets a 2-1 lead in the fifth with a two-out RBI single against Tyler Boudreau. Juan then added a solo home run off Boudreau in the sixth to stretch the lead to 3-1.

Ware had kept Tampa quiet through three scoreless innings before the eighth-inning unraveling. He took the loss after allowing five runs over 3.2 innings, though all five were unearned.

Tampa reliever Jose M. Rodriguez earned the win after pitching a perfect seventh inning.

The Mets fell to 2-10 in the second half and 35-43 overall. Tampa improved to 11-3 in the second half and 46-34 overall.

The teams close their six-game series Sunday at Clover Park, with first pitch scheduled for 12:10 p.m. It will be Little League Day. Little leaguers who wear their jerseys will receive free admission and a gift courtesy of Holiday Inn Express.

cards.headline: Juno Beach considers fence replacement at JB-7 beach access after Colony Condos residents report trespassing problems
cards.teaser: A missing fence at a Juno Beach public beach access point is creating tension between Colony Condos residents and summer beachgoers, with a fix potentially costing the town thousands of dollars.
cards.body:
Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. Without it, only bushes separate the public access path from private land. Lori Hill, a Colony resident, said the problem peaks in summer with visitors parking in private spots and cutting through bushes with coolers, fishing rods and lawn chairs. Hill said residents used to confront trespassers but now call police because people get rude.

The dispute came before the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where a town official noted the town is not obligated to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested a lower-cost solution may be worth exploring, proposing a combination of split rail fencing and shrubs. Hill said residents are hopeful the town will put the fence back up so they can have their landscaping and private parking restored. The council agreed to take up the fence question as part of its upcoming budget discussions on July 15.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: The City of Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, marking the city as the only Florida winner this year.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach has been named one of only 10 U.S. communities to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The prestigious award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment, saying "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson attributed the award to the city's long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several civic participation programs including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98% completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, stating the award belongs to the entire community. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A rating with record 93.5% graduation rate
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the state for the third year in a row, with 143 district-operated schools rated A or B.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third consecutive year, reflecting strong student performance across all grade levels. Schools receive letter grades based on student performance on state tests, graduation rates and advanced coursework performance. This year, 143 district-operated schools, or 84 percent, were rated "A" or "B," up from 120 schools the previous year. The district achieved a record-setting 93.5 percent graduation rate. Additionally, 86 percent of seniors participated in college-level coursework through Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment courses. Superintendent Mike Burke said the rating reflects the district's commitment to sparking academic success and helping every student ignite their future.

S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach made a dramatic leap from a "C" rating to an "A" this year, one of four district schools to improve their grades. Principal Rona Tata, who has served 15 years as principal and five years as assistant principal, said the turnaround began three years ago when staff modified the school's early childhood curriculum program for students starting at age 3 through kindergarten. Those students are now in third grade and performing at higher levels. Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary also improved from "C" to "A" ratings this year.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4% this year, hamburgers and buns among biggest increases
cards.teaser: According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago.
cards.body:
This year's Fourth of July cookouts will cost significantly more than last year. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The price increases are driven largely by inflation across multiple food categories. Ground beef prices have risen 5.5%, while buns are up 7.7%. Strawberries, affected by a Florida frost, have seen the steepest increase at 12.4%. Ice cream prices are also up 5.3% compared to last year.

Not all cookout staples have become more expensive. Potato prices are down this year, offering savings for those planning potato chips or salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can provide the best deals. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends strategies to manage costs. She suggests comparing prices across stores to find the best deals on your grocery list and emphasizes that cutting down food waste is critical for families. Woroch notes that meal planning is the key to reducing waste and controlling expenses.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie expands Midway Road, adds Florida Turnpike interchange to ease congestion
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved giving 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange coming to Florida's Turnpike on Midway Road.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange coming to Florida's Turnpike in St. Lucie County. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the interchange is about accessibility and keeping up with growth in the city. There is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie, Samples said. The interchange will accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. According to the FDOT website for the project, the second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase and construction is anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also working on improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange for the Turnpike.

Port St. Lucie resident Erin Scheumeister said the construction can be annoying but believes it is necessary. We definitely needed it to be expanded, Scheumeister said. It will be a lot better and easier to get to work. FDOT said the Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths, along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce into artistic destination with global artists
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain in Fort Pierce while connecting local and international artists through an artist-in-residency program.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination by preserving the historic Crain Estate and connecting local and international artists. The non-profit organization honors the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, who once lived on the property. Jaxson Crain was a tile worker whose craftsmanship is visible throughout the facility, from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. The estate remains approximately 90 percent unchanged from the Crains' time there, including details like the smoking and bourbon room with its man paneling and prestained glass. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate, including a gazebo shipped from India that features tiny peacocks in its design.

The Peacock House gets its name from the birds that have roamed the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, starting with seven birds that have since grown to over 100. Among the flock is Bob, a beloved bird believed to be 60 years old and the oldest peacock on the property, who walks with a limp and is hand-fed daily. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world and offers simple but elegant accommodations. The art lab provides classes for children and adults of all skill levels, including one-on-one instruction in mediums like sculpting and watercolor.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community rallies around man who lost fiance in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside a Hobe Sound home. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance rebuild.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her home in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause, though the fire remains under investigation. Nina Fenn, who had been White's friend for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from White's fiancé Mark. "We received a call from Mark stating that Misty had passed away in a fire," Fenn said.

Friends have launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Fenn described White as a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, piano, and people. "She was always the first to lend a hand," Fenn said. The loss is compounded by previous grief Mark has endured. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically," Fenn said. Adding to the heartbreak, White's birthday was July 4, meaning she died just days before turning a year older. "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County marine deputies rescue two boaters after vessel sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit rescued two boaters Wednesday after their small motorized boat sank in the Intracoastal Waterway. Both were wearing life jackets.
cards.body:
Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, thanks to a quick response from St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit deputies and the life-saving decision to wear life jackets. The Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged on July 1. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded.

Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but deputies say they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived. Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. "This incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life," the sheriff's office said in a Facebook post. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call."

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes Monday for $3 million renovation that doubles boat capacity
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a year-long renovation project expected to be completed by next Fourth of July. The $3 million improvement, funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees, will nearly double the facility's capacity from 18 slips to 44 slips that accommodate both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation includes construction of a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock, and a smaller floating platform. With more than 1,400 boaters using the dock annually, Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades address storm resilience concerns. "They're doing it to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms," Reed said. "So the year of waiting will be worth it."

Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates passenger tours from the dock, initially worried about maintaining operations during construction. The city worked out a solution allowing the company to build a gate at the non-floating section of the dock for customer boarding. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, appreciated the accommodation and emphasized the dock's importance to Stuart. "Stuart is not Stuart without the water," Kuyrkendall said. He noted current limitations, particularly on busy weekends when finding available docking spots becomes difficult, and called the modernization project "really going to be great for the city but also for us as well."

hero.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles with sister Venus due to knee injury
hero.teaser: Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday because of a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week.
hero.body:
Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week. The 44-year-old lost 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3 to 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia on Tuesday. In an Instagram post, Serena said she was "heartbroken to have to withdraw from doubles" and that playing alongside Venus "meant the world to me." She added: "I did everything I could but unfortunately my knee just isn't ready to compete."

The post included images of four syringes showing fluid drained from her knee after the singles match, along with a video of her walking with strapping on her right leg and what appeared to be one of her daughters holding a cane for her. The Williams sisters were scheduled to face Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra in a first-round match that had been pushed back to give Serena more recovery time. The 46-year-old Venus played in mixed doubles on Friday with Kevin Krawietz, losing to Tereza Mihalikova and Lloyd Glasspool. With the U.S. Open approaching, Serena indicated she could compete again soon, saying "stay tuned to a city near you." The Williams sisters are six-time Wimbledon women's doubles champions as partners.

cards.headline: Argentina survives Cape Verde scare 3-2 in World Cup Round of 16 thriller
cards.teaser: Defending World Cup champion Argentina defeated Cape Verde 3-2 in extra time on Friday to advance to the Round of 16.
cards.body:
Lionel Messi and Argentina beat Cape Verde 3-2 on Friday and advanced to the World Cup Round of 16 in a match where the tiny island nation challenged the reigning champion until the final minutes of extra time. The go-ahead score for Argentina was credited as an own-goal after Cristian Romero's header deflected off Cape Verde's Diney Borges in the 111th minute.

Messi scored early in regulation with his record-extending 20th career World Cup goal, sneaking behind the Cape Verde defense on a well-timed run as Martinez lofted a pass toward him in the 29th minute. Lisandro Martinez scored in the 103rd minute to put Argentina ahead 2-1. Sidny Lopes Cabral and Deroy Duarte scored for Cape Verde, both equalizers that stunned the pro-Argentina crowd in South Florida.

Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, 40 years old, had 10 saves against Argentina, including five against Messi. Argentina will face Egypt in Atlanta on Tuesday after Egypt beat Australia in a penalty shootout earlier Friday. Messi now has seven goals in this tournament, one more than France's Kylian Mbapp in the Golden Boot race, and has scored 12 goals during his record eight-match scoring streak.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football program is setting its sights on a state championship heading into the 2026 fall season. After finishing last year with a 10-2 record and a district title, the team's second-round playoff exit has fueled their ambitions for deeper postseason success. Head coach Jimmy Robertson highlighted the importance of his senior class, noting that most are four-year seniors who came through the middle school program. "They know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said.

To elevate their competitive level, the Scots have intentionally scheduled stronger opponents for the upcoming season. Senior Jack Williams explained the reasoning behind this approach, saying the team wants to test itself against quality competition to advance to the next level and attract new talent. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that playoff advancement is the primary measure of success, stating that going further in the postseason is what matters most. Fellow senior Edmyer St. Jean viewed the summer workouts as motivation for the challenges ahead, saying the daily effort adds up toward breaking their record when the season begins.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Let Late Lead Slip Away in 10-3 Loss to Tarpons
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie Mets were six outs away from ending their losing streak Saturday before a disastrous eighth inning turned a 3-1 lead into a 10-3 loss to the Tampa Tarpons at Clover P
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets were six outs away from ending their losing streak Saturday before a disastrous eighth inning turned a 3-1 lead into a 10-3 loss to the Tampa Tarpons at Clover Park.

Tampa scored six unearned runs in the eighth inning, capitalizing on four Mets errors, then added three more runs in the ninth to pull away on Independence Day. The Tarpons extended their winning streak to eight games, while St. Lucie dropped its ninth straight.

The Mets led 3-1 entering the eighth after building the advantage with timely offense and strong relief work. But Tampa's comeback began after Hans Montero reached and eventually scored the tying run when Bryce Martin-Grudzielanek hit a two-out ground ball to third baseman Branny De Oleo. The ball deflected off De Oleo's glove for an error, allowing Montero to come home and even the game at 3-3.

The inning continued from there, and David McCann delivered the decisive blow with a three-run home run off Conner Ware to give Tampa a 6-3 lead. McCann struck again in the ninth, launching another three-run homer off Luis Alvarez to make it 10-3.

McCann finished 3-for-4 with two home runs, a single, a walk and seven RBI. The performance came one day after he went 0-for-4 with four strikeouts.

St. Lucie had trailed 1-0 early before tying the game in the fourth inning on an RBI groundout by Simon Juan. Chase Meggers gave the Mets a 2-1 lead in the fifth with a two-out RBI single against Tyler Boudreau. Juan then added a solo home run off Boudreau in the sixth to stretch the lead to 3-1.

Ware had kept Tampa quiet through three scoreless innings before the eighth-inning unraveling. He took the loss after allowing five runs over 3.2 innings, though all five were unearned.

Tampa reliever Jose M. Rodriguez earned the win after pitching a perfect seventh inning.

The Mets fell to 2-10 in the second half and 35-43 overall. Tampa improved to 11-3 in the second half and 46-34 overall.

The teams close their six-game series Sunday at Clover Park, with first pitch scheduled for 12:10 p.m. It will be Little League Day. Little leaguers who wear their jerseys will receive free admission and a gift courtesy of Holiday Inn Express.

hero.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach Offers Sea Turtle Nesting Season Programs Through September
hero.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering a variety of educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season this summer. Guests can participate in seasonal experiences through September, including guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. The programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn more about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The center's Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations during the programs may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups continue encouraging beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

cards.headline: North Palm Beach Celebrates Independence Day with Fireworks and America 250 Events
cards.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors celebrated Independence Day with family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
cards.body:
Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County. The free community event included a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m.

The festivities began with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests could enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families could take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games.

Live music from Solstice Reign began around 6 p.m. Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course offered one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse also hosted a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

hero.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion Florida budget with $810 million in vetoes
hero.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion state budget this week, marking the fourth consecutive year of shrinking spending plans. The term-limited Governor vetoed nearly $810 million in line-item appropriations, along with blocking another $750 million the Legislature wanted to transfer into the state's rainy-day fund.

DeSantis said he vetoed items he considered either inappropriate or nice to have, declining to match his record-breaking $3.1 billion veto total from 2022. The budget includes billions for accelerating road construction projects, increasing teacher pay, and making major investments in cancer research. The spending plan also sets aside $665 million for Everglades restoration. Among the notable cuts, DeSantis vetoed $91.5 million intended to increase correctional officer salaries.

Government watchdog Florida TaxWatch had urged DeSantis to eliminate 621 projects worth $830 million that the group labeled budget turkeys. DeSantis ultimately vetoed 184 of the 621 appropriations the organization wanted cut. The Legislature passed a proposed constitutional amendment last year that would increase the mandated cap on the budget stabilization fund, prompting lawmakers this year to add the $750 million transfer to prepare for the new requirement.

DeSantis also indicated he would not formally lead any political committee to campaign for a proposed amendment after the Legislature changed his original proposal. He said he might participate if asked but would not spearhead the effort himself. The new fiscal year budget represents DeSantis's final spending plan as Governor.

cards.headline: Southwest Florida communities celebrate America's 250th with fireworks and parades
cards.teaser: Cities across Southwest Florida hosted Fourth of July festivities including fireworks displays, drone shows, and waterfront celebrations marking the semiquincentennial.
cards.body:
Southwest Florida communities are celebrating America's 250th birthday with a full slate of Independence Day events. Bradenton and Palmetto are marking the semiquincentennial together with festivities on both sides of the Manatee River, including activities along the Bradenton Riverwalk, Rossi Park, Old Main Street, and Palmetto's Riverside Park. Palmetto's 15th annual Fourth Fest at Riverside Park will feature 14 food trucks, 20 artisan and community vendors, a "Lil Firecrackers" kids zone, and live music, with fireworks visible from both sides of the river. Sarasota's bayfront will host its America250 fireworks display beginning at 9 p.m.

Additional celebrations span the region from Sarasota to Fort Myers Beach. Venice will hold a patriotic parade through Historic Downtown Venice starting at 9:30 a.m., followed by a fireworks show at the South Jetty scheduled between 9 and 9:15 p.m., with July 5 as a rain date. Siesta Beach will host its 35th annual community fireworks show from 8 to 9:30 p.m., funded entirely by local residents, businesses, and community supporters. Downtown Fort Myers will present a free concert by Deb The Dynamics and a combined fireworks and drone show at the Caloosa Sound Amphitheater from 7 to 9:30 p.m. Fort Myers Beach will hold a parade at 10 a.m. starting at Bay Oaks Recreation Center and continuing down Estero Boulevard to Times Square, followed by fireworks launched from a barge near Times Square around 9 p.m.

hero.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation preserves Crain Estate history, offers artist residencies in Fort Pierce
hero.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is establishing Fort Pierce as an artistic hub by preserving the historic Crain Estate and fostering connections between local and international artists. Operating from the former home of Jaxson and Mary Crain, the non-profit organization maintains the couple's legacy while serving the community. Jaxson Crain's work as a tile craftsman is evident throughout the property, with his tiling visible across floors, walls, and ceilings. Visitors can explore the lush gardens and distinctive architecture through guided tours offered Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays. The home's original character remains largely intact, including spaces like the smoking and bourbon room, which features wood paneling, masculine decor, and decorative stained glass that opens onto the front patio bar. According to Krystal Masters, the art director, approximately 90 percent of the estate looks exactly as it did when the Crains lived there.

The Crains were collectors who traveled internationally nine times, bringing back unique treasures for their Florida property. Among their acquisitions is a gazebo shipped from India that is adorned with small peacock designs, which the foundation is currently restoring. The foundation has deliberately chosen to preserve the estate's original character rather than commercialize it. The property's name derives from the peacocks that have inhabited the grounds for decades. The Crains brought seven peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, and the population has since grown to over 100 birds. One notable resident is Bob, a peacock believed to be 60 years old and identifiable by his distinctive limp. Bob enjoys celebrity status at the estate, complete with his own designated living space, personal bowls, and daily hand-feeding by staff members. Tour guides note that interactions between young visitors and the peacocks create memorable experiences, particularly when the birds eat from children's hands.

The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts creative professionals from around the world, providing simple yet elegant accommodations on the property. The on-site art lab serves as a creative hub offering classes for both children and adults without requiring prior professional experience. Masters teaches one-on-one classes specifically designed for complete beginners, helping students create finished artwork during their first session. The lab offers various mediums including sculpting and watercolor painting, with specialized workshops such as "paint your pet in watercolor and rainbow."

For Masters, art extends beyond artistic expression into therapeutic practice. "Art is a form of therapy and it distresses people," she explains. Students leave the classes feeling fulfilled and engaged rather than preoccupied with their phones. This approach to teaching, combined with the foundation's commitment to preserving the Crains' legacy while building community connections, demonstrates how the Peacock House Art Foundation successfully blends historical preservation with contemporary artistic programming.
